meta.tagline: Ionian turquoise, lagoon mussels and the pearl of the Albanian Riviera

pills: The pearl of the Albanian Riviera

overview.title: Welcome to Ksamil
overview.intro: Ksamil is a small headland on the map, but the colour of its water could make a continent jealous: here the Ionian turns Caribbean, four little islands sit within swimming distance, and the silhouette of Corfu stretches across the strait. On one side lie Butrint's two-thousand-year-old stones, on the other the mussel lines of the lagoon. This is not a polished resort but a fast-growing fishing village — a little untidy, deeply warm-hearted, and still the most honestly priced clear water in the Mediterranean. Come avash avash: hurry has no place in the language of these coves.

local_word.definition: 'Slowly, slowly': a phrase that passed from Ottoman Turkish into Albanian and sums up the tempo of the coastal towns. The waiter and the boatman give the same answer — avash avash. Adopt it and your holiday starts sooner.

rules.title: Into the sea early, into the shade at noon
rules.description: In July and August the coves fill after 11 and the sunbeds run out: between 8 and 10 the water is like glass and the beach half empty. Take a long lunch at midday and return for the late-afternoon swim — that is the island rhythm.

rules.title: Get used to two currencies
rules.description: The official money is the lek, but the euro also speaks fluently on this coast: clarify which currency a price is quoted in, and your change may come back in lek. Keep the exchange rate ready on your phone — confusion is the most expensive tip.

rules.title: Make Ksamil the base, collect the surroundings
rules.description: The magic here is in the radius: Butrint 10 minutes, the Blue Eye half an hour, Sarandë 20 minutes, Corfu across the water by ferry. Whoever never leaves the sunbed sees the riviera's richest corner only by half.

quick_facts.label: Getting there
quick_facts.sub: Ferry to Sarandë ~30 min · Tirana 4 hrs

quick_facts.label: Around the area
quick_facts.sub: The Sarandë line runs all day

quick_facts.label: Language
quick_facts.sub: English and Italian common on the coast

tip.label: The Ksamil philosophy
tip.text: In Ksamil the plan is one line: which cove, at what hour? The sea arranges the rest. If the famous beach is full, the one two coves over always exists — this headland hides a dozen coves within walking distance.

transport.title: Getting Around
transport.intro: Ksamil is small and its surroundings generous: furgons, scooters and boats are this headland's three wheels.

items.title: Arriving via Corfu
items.description: The most practical route is flying to Corfu and taking the Sarandë ferry from the port: you're in Albania in half an hour. There's passport control — book the ferry ahead in season.

items.title: The Sarandë–Ksamil furgons
items.description: Minibuses shuttle the coast road all day: cheap, frequent and used to beach bags. The Butrint-bound line passes through Ksamil — raise a hand to board, say the word to get off.

items.title: A scooter — the key to the coves
items.description: For the hidden coves and the Blue Eye a scooter is freedom: the roads are short but winding, and the helmet is not negotiable. Rent early in summer, park in the shade.

items.title: The village on foot
items.description: No walk from the centre to the farthest beach exceeds 20 minutes: the paths drop to the coves through olive groves. Sandals over flip-flops — the paths are stony.

items.title: Boats and kayaks
items.description: Small boats from the beaches hop to the islands and neighbouring coves; renting a kayak and rounding the four islands at your own paddling rhythm is the morning's best plan. Fix the price before boarding.

callout.label: Ferry tip
callout.text: Return from Corfu on the sunset crossing: as the sun drops over the Ionian, the Sarandë bay turns orange — one of the Mediterranean's best view cruises for the price of a ferry ticket.

stay.title: Where to Stay
stay.intro: In Ksamil the question is distance: zero metres to the beach, a view from the hills, or Sarandë's buzz?

local_word.definition: A family-run guesthouse: Albanian hospitality turned into lodging. Homemade jam at breakfast, a raki offered in the courtyard at night — whoever stays in a bujtina sees more than whoever stays in a hotel.

items.name: Ksamil centre
items.description: Walking distance to the main beaches and restaurants: lively in summer, busy in the evenings. Mostly apartments and small hotels — the right address if the beach comes first.

items.name: The southern coves front
items.description: Hillside hotels towards Mirror Beach and Pema e Thatë: terraces looking down on turquoise coves, quiet nights. A car or scooter makes life easier.

items.name: The lagoon side
items.description: Guesthouses facing the Butrint lagoon: mussel farms, birdsong and sunrise mist. Far from the beach crowds, close to nature — for those who put peace first.

items.name: Sarandë
items.description: The town 20 minutes north: a long promenade, nightlife, the ferry port and a wide hotel range. Hopping to Ksamil by furgon is easy — for those after evening motion.

items.name: The Ksamil hills
items.description: Slope apartments above the village: minutes to both the centre and the coves, prices friendlier than the seafront. A Corfu sunset from the balcony comes as a bonus in most rooms.

best_time.title: When to Go
best_time.intro: The Ionian sun is generous: May to October is one long summer, July-August a full stage, and winter a silent headland left to the locals.

items.label: Spring
items.name: The Season's Gate
items.subtitle: Spring · Empty coves, opening terraces
items.description: In May the sea is cool but swimmable and the coves nearly empty; June is the peak of balance — everything open, the crowds still on their way. Butrint and the Blue Eye are at their finest in this light.

callout.label: June tip
callout.text: Come in the first half of June: sunbeds without haggling, clear water, tables waiting at the restaurants. These are the riviera's two smartest weeks.

items.label: Summer
items.name: Turquoise Peak
items.subtitle: Summer · Full beaches, warm nights
items.description: The region's two busiest months: the coves fill, the evenings stretch, the prices climb. The sea is magnificent, but a morning strategy is essential — the early bird finds the postcard, the late one finds the crowd.

callout.label: August note
callout.text: In August reach the famous beaches before 9, escape to the lagoon side or Butrint at midday, and return for the late swim. Ask the sunbed price before lying down — the front row has its own tariff.

items.label: Autumn
items.name: Warm Sea, Empty Coves
items.subtitle: Autumn · September, the golden month
items.description: September belongs to those in the know: the sea holds summer's warmth, the crowds have receded, the prices have dropped. Swimming is still possible in October; by November the headland returns to its winter silence.

callout.label: September tip
callout.text: In September kayak to the islands and finish the afternoon at Butrint: you'll be nearly alone in the ancient theatre — none of the summer queues remain.

items.label: Winter
items.name: The Silent Headland
items.subtitle: Winter · Closed season, local life
items.description: Most hotels close and the village returns to itself: the olive harvest, the mussel stalls, the empty coves. Not for a beach holiday, but the Butrint + Sarandë combination is still lovely on mild winter days.

callout.label: Winter note
callout.text: If you come in winter, spend a sunny noon at Lëkurësi Castle: the Sarandë bay, the Ksamil headland and Corfu in one frame — whatever the season, this view never goes off duty.

eat.title: What to Eat
eat.intro: The Ksamil table draws from two sources: the Butrint lagoon's mussels and the Ionian's daily catch — with the village bakery and raki alongside.

local_word.definition: Mussels: the Butrint lagoon holds some of the Mediterranean's oldest mussel farms, and this is the Ksamil table's signature. Steamed, with garlic or pan-fried — the fresh ones come up in the morning and are gone by night.

items.name: Butrint mussels
items.description: The lagoon's mussels are small, sweet and intense: steamed in white wine is the classic, served near-raw with lemon the brave choice. The price per kilo is a friendly surprise — order until you're full.

items.name: The day's fish on the grill
items.description: Sea bass, bream, or whatever the morning net brought: chosen by the kilo, grilled over coals, served with olive oil and lemon. Ask the price before the scales — that is the custom.
items.tag: Choose from the display · by weight

items.name: Grilled octopus
items.description: Octopus sun-dried and finished over coals is the pride of the shore restaurants: smoky outside, tender inside. With rocket and a cold white — the crowned plate of a beach afternoon.
items.tag: At a shore restaurant · over coals

items.name: A byrek morning
items.description: Hand-rolled pastry with spinach, cheese or minced meat: bought hot from the bakery, eaten standing. A byrek + dhallë (the local ayran) — the native formula for a pre-beach breakfast.
items.tag: Hot from the bakery · with dhallë

items.name: Fërgesë and the village plates
items.description: Peppers, tomatoes and curd cheese meeting in a clay dish: Albanian home cooking in summary. If you see tavë kosi (lamb baked in yoghurt), don't hesitate — the interior's classic has come down to the coast.
items.tag: Home cooking · in the clay dish

items.name: The raki ritual and local wine
items.description: Grape raki is the official language of the pre-dinner offering: in a small glass, with a 'Gëzuar!'. Albanian winemaking is rising too — ask, and try a local bottle.

callout.label: The restaurant rule
callout.text: Tables at zero metres from the sand charge a view tax; walk one row back or towards the lagoon. 'What did the net bring today?' is the sentence that opens a good restaurant's door — if the answer is rehearsed, keep walking; if it's fresh, sit down.

hidden_gems.title: Hidden Corners
hidden_gems.intro: Everyone knows the main beach; these six are the headland's concealed face.

items.name: The ancient city of Butrint
items.description: The UNESCO site at the lagoon's end: a Greek theatre, Roman baths, a Byzantine baptistery and a Venetian tower in the shade of one forest. Enter at the first hour — among the stones, just the tortoises and you.

items.name: Syri i Kaltër — the Blue Eye
items.description: An ice-blue spring surging from deep underground: its true depth has never been fully measured. The water is 10 degrees — diving is banned, but the spectacle is free. Go early and skip the midday queue.

items.name: Plazhi i Pasqyrave — Mirror Beach
items.description: A small cove hidden among the cliffs on the Sarandë road: the water so still it takes its name from a mirror. The stair descent filters the crowds — at an early hour it's nearly a private beach.

items.name: Pema e Thatë
items.description: The 'Dry Tree' beach: a long calm strand at Ksamil's southern tip, reached through pine and olive. Corfu straight ahead — the crowds far behind.

items.name: Sunset at Lëkurësi Castle
items.description: The Ottoman castle above Sarandë: the bay, the Ksamil headland, Corfu and the Greek mountains behind, all from one terrace. Go up for sunset with a glass in hand — this is the riviera's balcony.

items.rarity: An island tour to the sound of oars
items.name: The four islands by kayak
items.description: The finest way to Ksamil's islets is a kayak: pass cove by cove, land on deserted pebble strips, snorkel the rocks. No engine noise, no queue — the reward of 8 am.

callout.label: Cove tip
callout.text: Every famous beach in Ksamil has a nameless neighbour: walk the path five minutes on, and the next pebble strip is usually half empty. The sea is the same sea — the difference is only in the name.

traps.title: Tourist Traps
traps.intro: Ksamil is warm-hearted, but its tourism grew fast; these four protect your budget and your day.

items.name: Lying down on a sunbed without asking
items.description: In August the front-row sunbed sets ask serious euros, and once you've sat down the haggling is over.
items.instead: Ask the price before lying down, or spread your towel in the free zone. Arrive before 9 am and on most beaches you'll take the front row at the normal price.

items.name: Losing change in the currency shuffle
items.description: Pay in euros, receive change in lek, and the rate gets 'rounded'; small differences add up to a plump invisible bill by day's end.
items.instead: Pay in lek where possible, keep the rate on your phone, and count your change. An ATM's lek is usually better than the beachfront rate.

items.name: Getting into a taxi without a price
items.description: Short hops are quoted at season prices; on routes like the Blue Eye a 'waiting fee' is added afterwards.
items.instead: Fix the total — waiting included — before getting in, or use the furgon + scooter pair; both cost less than half.

items.name: Going to the Blue Eye at noon
items.description: At midday the car park overflows, the path becomes a queue and you stand selfie-watch at the spring.
items.instead: Go at the first hour or after 5 pm: the water just as blue, the forest cool, the platform empty. Stop at a village restaurant on the way back — real prices, no tourist menu.

callout.label: Golden rule
callout.text: In Ksamil no summer price is learned without asking: sunbed, boat, taxi — a smiling 'sa kushton?' (how much?) is this coast's most valuable sentence.

itinerary.title: Ready-Made Routes
itinerary.intro: If you hate planning, follow these flows. The times are flexible; keep the spirit, break the order.

plans.title: If You Have 1 Day
plans.subtitle: A full dose of riviera, from turquoise to ancient stone

steps.title: The morning sea
steps.description: The first swim in the main cove while the water is glass: sunbeds empty, light soft. Breakfast of byrek + coffee from the shore bakery.

steps.title: The islands by kayak
steps.description: Rent a kayak and round the four islands cove by cove: land on a deserted pebble strip, snorkel the rocks.

steps.title: A mussel table
steps.description: Lunch on the lagoon side: steamed Butrint mussels + grilled fish + a cold white. Avash avash — no hurry.

steps.title: The stones of Butrint
steps.description: Ten minutes down the road and two thousand years back: the theatre, the mosaics and the Venetian tower over the lagoon. The forest's shade is the afternoon's friend.

steps.title: The Lëkurësi sunset
steps.description: Up to the castle: as bay, headland and Corfu turn orange, raise your glass — you're on the riviera's best balcony.

steps.title: An evening on the shore
steps.description: Dinner at a fish restaurant in the centre, then a slow close in the beach bars: a Ksamil night is calm and starry.

plans.title: If You Have 3 Days
plans.subtitle: Coves, ancient cities and an island escape

steps.title: Classic Ksamil
steps.description: The one-day flow above: morning sea, islands, mussels, Butrint, Lëkurësi.

steps.title: Cove hunting and the Blue Eye
steps.description: The Blue Eye early in the morning; down the Mirror Beach stairs on the way back; the late afternoon in Pema e Thatë's calm, then an evening walk and dinner on the Sarandë promenade.

steps.title: A Corfu escape or the deeper riviera
steps.description: A day trip to Corfu by ferry (old town + fortress), or a northern route: Porto Palermo castle and Borsh beach. One last sunset swim on return — let the farewell be salty.

phrases.title: 5-Word Survival Kit
phrases.intro: Albanian is full of words that wink at its neighbours; these five, joined with a smile, open every door.

items.meaning: Hello — 'tungjatjeta' or the casual 'ç'kemi' work too
Thank you — long, but the effect is great; texted simply as 'flm'
Please / you're welcome — the key of courtesy
Cheers! — eye contact as the raki rises is mandatory
'How much?' — from sunbed to boat, this coast's most functional question
